recentItems.title: Russian Oil Refinery and Almaz-Antey plant hit: meanwhile, Ukraine receives a decision on Patriot
recentItems.description:
Several Russian regions came under drone attack during the night of September 25. In Perm, a fire was reported near one of Russia’s largest oil refineries. In Ulyanovsk, the target was the Iskra plant, which is linked to the Almaz-Antey concern. In Voronezh, a fire broke out at a major synthetic-rubber manufacturing facility.

Against this backdrop, Russia continues its attacks on Ukraine, with Kyiv coming under another strike. At the same time, important news emerged concerning Ukraine’s air defense: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Donald Trump had made a final decision to grant Ukraine licenses to produce missiles for Patriot systems. The exact timeline and scale of the future production have not yet been publicly announced.

The episode also covers negotiations on a possible energy and maritime ceasefire, the Kremlin’s position, U.S. sanctions pressure, preparations for a special tribunal, and the prospect of trilateral contacts between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia.

recentItems.title: UKRAINE APPLIES PRESSURE ON THREE AXES: “VIVALDI” success, strikes on Moscow and targets in Crimea
recentItems.description:
Operation «Vivaldi» is continuing in northern Donetsk region. The Third Army Corps reported the liberation of Shandryholove and Derylove, as well as the establishment of full control over Drobysheve. During the two stages of the operation, 125 square kilometers of territory were returned to Ukrainian control, including 50 square kilometers that were directly liberated. Ukrainian forces are using artillery, drones, and ground robotic systems in an effort to disrupt Russian command and control, logistics, and supplies in the Lyman direction.

The episode also covers the consequences of the large-scale attack on Moscow: the Moscow Oil Refinery halted crude-oil processing after fires broke out at two main processing units, while operations at the capital’s airports experienced major disruptions. We also examine Ukrainian strikes on military and logistical infrastructure in occupied Crimea, the strengthening of Ukraine’s air defenses ahead of winter, new interceptor drones, the situation along key sectors of the front, and European intelligence assessments of Russian hybrid threats to NATO countries.

recentItems.title: MOSCOW OIL REFINERY HALTS OPERATIONS AFTER ATTACK: three more plants hit, Russian aircraft damaged
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian long-range strikes this week targeted several key sites linked to Russia’s military and fuel infrastructure. Following the September 20 attack, the Moscow Oil Refinery halted crude-oil processing. Reuters reported that fires broke out at both of the refinery’s main primary processing units, and repairs could take several weeks. During this period, other Russian oil-refining facilities also came under attack.

Another major target was Russia’s Nebo-U long-range radar system. Soldiers from the Phoenix border unit reported disabling the station in a precision drone strike. The radar is estimated to be worth approximately $100 million and is designed to detect and track aerial targets over long distances.

In Rostov-on-Don, long-range drones operated by the SBU’s Alpha Special Operations Center attacked the Rostov-Central military airfield. The Security Service of Ukraine claimed that an An-12, two An-26 aircraft, and three helicopters were hit. A large fire, followed by secondary detonations, broke out at the aircraft parking area.

The report also examines Ukraine’s reported Russian military losses over the past week, the estimated value of destroyed artillery and air-defense systems, and how these losses are affecting the capabilities of Russian forces. Another focus is the new generation of Ukrainian interceptor drones capable of chasing down and destroying high-speed Russian jet-powered UAVs.

recentItems.title: CAN THE ABRAMS SURVIVE FPV DRONES? Ukrainian tank crews show its protection and interior
recentItems.description:
How is the American Abrams being adapted to the realities of modern warfare, where FPV drones have become one of the main threats to armored vehicles? Servicemembers of the 225th Separate Assault Regiment show their tank from the outside and inside and explain how the crew reinforced its protection on their own.

The vehicle has been fitted with additional metal structures that the soldiers call “hedgehogs,” as well as explosive reactive armor. Special attention was paid to the tracks and running gear: damage to these components can immobilize a heavy tank even without penetrating its main armor. The crew explains how the additional structures are intended to counter conventional FPV drones and fiber-optic-controlled UAVs.

We also take a look inside the Abrams, including the driver’s, gunner’s, and loader’s positions, the thermal imaging sight, the backup aiming system, the onboard computer, and the 120 mm gun. The tank crews talk about the 1,500-horsepower engine, fuel consumption, the vehicle’s speed, and the specifics of operating this heavy machine.

recentItems.title: KYIV UNDER FIRE: Ukraine strikes Russian refineries & missile plants, Zelenskyy on the Patriot
recentItems.description:
Russia continues its series of attacks on Kyiv. On September 25, Russian drones struck residential and non-residential sites across the capital. As a result of the morning attacks, the number of injured rose to 20, while a 14-year-old teenager was killed. A high-rise residential building, private homes, garages, and the building of the High Council of Justice were damaged. Later that day, a Russian drone struck an office building in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi District, killing four people. Other regions of Ukraine also came under attack. In Zaporizhzhia, Russian drones targeted medical facilities, forcing the evacuation of patients. In Odesa region, private homes, warehouses, vehicles, and other civilian infrastructure were damaged. The report includes testimonies from people who survived the attacks, the work of emergency responders, and the aftermath of the strikes.

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s Defense Forces reported new long-range strikes on targets in Russia. The reported targets included oil refineries in Perm and Novoshakhtinsk, as well as three facilities connected to the production of Russian missile weapons. These reportedly included a plant in Ulyanovsk and facilities in Tula and Voronezh regions. The report also examines the situation on the front line, Ukraine’s reported Russian military losses, and the fighting along the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and other axes.

recentItems.title: UKRAINE STRIKES A DRONE DEAL — New Agreement with Finland as Russia Tries to Save Its Remaining Oil
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian drones continue to strike Russian military and energy infrastructure. Damage to an oil depot was reported in Rostov Region, while a fire broke out at an industrial facility in Krasnodar Krai. Another key topic is the “Crimean Switch Off” operation conducted by Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces. According to Commander Robert Brovdi, over the course of two and a half months, Ukrainian forces targeted 412 energy facilities in Russia and in temporarily occupied territories.

During the night of September 24, Kyiv came under a Russian attack involving ballistic missiles and drones. According to the city authorities, two people were killed and eight others were injured. The damaged sites included a maternity hospital, private homes, warehouses, and vehicles.

Meanwhile, the sixth Crimea Platform Summit took place in New York. It brought together representatives from more than 60 countries. Zelenskyy said that the current level of representation was the broadest in the six years since the format was launched. Participants discussed Crimea, international pressure on Russia, human rights, Black Sea security, and further international steps.

recentItems.title: BIRTH UNDER BALLISTIC ATTACK: Russia’s Massive Strike and Zelenskyy’s Talks on Patriot Systems
recentItems.description:
Russia launched another combined attack on Ukraine using Zircon missiles, ballistic missiles, and 282 drones of various types. According to Ukraine’s Air Force, Ukrainian air defence destroyed or suppressed 227 aerial targets. The main directions of the attack were Kyiv and Odesa regions. People were killed and others were injured in Kyiv during the overnight ballistic attack. Residential and civilian facilities were damaged, including Maternity Hospital No. 2. At the time of the attack, patients and medical staff were sheltering underground — and it was there, at 2:05 a.m., that a baby boy was born.

The Kharkiv, Odesa, Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, and Zhytomyr regions also came under attack. This episode covers the aftermath of the strikes, the situation at the front — where Ukraine’s General Staff recorded 277 combat engagements — as well as attacks by the Defence Forces on two Russian radar stations and a launch site for attack drones. Another key topic is Ukraine’s protection against ballistic missiles. Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Mark Rutte discussed the consequences of Russian strikes and the needs of Ukraine’s air defence.
